title: Rain in Tokyo
author: Tadoku Note (original)
summary: 傘を忘れた雨の夕方。見知らぬ老人が「一緒に駅まで」と声をかけてくれました。

source.note: Original text written for this app.

paragraphs: It was a Monday in June. Yuki left her apartment at seven thirty. The sky was gray, but she did not look at it. She was thinking about her meeting at ten o’clock.
She took the train to Shinjuku. The train was full, as always. She stood near the door and read the news on her phone.
At six in the evening, Yuki finished work. She went down to the street. It was raining hard. People opened their umbrellas, one after another, like flowers.
Yuki did not have an umbrella. She remembered the gray sky that morning. “Oh, no,” she said quietly.
The station was five minutes away. Five minutes in this rain was a long time. She waited under the roof of the building. The rain did not stop. It got stronger.
An old man stood next to her. He had a large black umbrella. He looked at the rain, and then he looked at Yuki.
“Are you going to the station?” he asked. “Yes,” Yuki said. “Then let’s walk together,” he said. “This umbrella is big enough for two.”
Yuki was surprised, but she said, “Thank you very much.” They walked to the station under the black umbrella. The man walked slowly, so Yuki walked slowly too.

“I worked near here for forty years,” the man said. “Every June, it rains like this. Every June, someone forgets an umbrella.” He laughed. “Once, it was me. A young woman shared her umbrella with me. That was a long time ago.”
At the station, the man closed his umbrella. Yuki thanked him again. “Please,” he said, “next time, you can share yours with someone.”

The next week, it rained again. This time Yuki had her umbrella. At six o’clock, she went down to the street. A young man was standing under the roof. He looked at the rain. He did not have an umbrella.
Yuki smiled. “Are you going to the station?” she asked.
